info.title: Konklav control plane
info.description: Every operation's `x-konklav-capability` names the capability its caller needs. The bootstrap token and `konklav:control:all` hold them all. A batch (`POST /v1/batch`) needs none of its own: each of its operations needs the capability it needs alone.

post.summary: Applies operations in order, all or nothing.
post.description:
Each operation is a `PUT`, `POST` or `DELETE` with the path (without
`/v1`) and body it takes alone, and is authorized against the caller's own
capabilities. On success, `results` holds what each answered; on failure
nothing is committed and the error is the failing operation's, with its
position as `error.operation`. With an `idempotency_key`, repeating the
batch answers what it first answered, with new secrets where that answer
showed some.

200.description: Every operation was applied, now or by the first batch with the same idempotency key

put.description: The whole catalog is replaced: actions and groups left out are removed.

Only local passwords and secret keys can be break-glass credentials. Every
use of one appends `break_glass.used`.

post.description:
Creates a new password credential that records the one it replaces. Sessions
established with the old one end. Idempotent on a caller-chosen `id`:
repeating the request with the same password returns 200.

200.description: Already replaced by this credential with the same password

post.description: Sessions established with the credential end.

put.description: Every session started with the credential carries these restrictive flags.

put.summary: Sets when one slot of a secret key expires.
put.description:
The slot keeps its secret; `null` makes it never expire. An expiry in the
past makes the slot's secret stop working at once.

post.summary: Rotates one slot of a secret key.
post.description:
Sets a new secret for the slot. The other slot keeps working, so clients can
switch over without downtime. The new secret is shown only once.

requestBody.description: Optional; without it the new secret never expires

200.description: Rotated. The slot's new secret is in `secret_key`, shown only once.

post.description:
Imports credentials from another system, with their existing hashes or
secrets, all or nothing.

TOTP seeds arrive in plaintext and are encrypted before they are stored. All
or nothing.
Imports sessions from another system, all or nothing.
Imports subjects from another system, all or nothing.

The invite token is delivered (as `delivery.requested`) and never returned.
Idempotent on a caller-chosen `id`: repeating the request with the same
content returns 200 and delivers nothing again.

200.description: Already existed with the same content; nothing is delivered again

201.description: Created; the token is delivered to the address, never returned

post.summary: Revokes an invite, so it can no longer be redeemed.

Revoking it again answers the same; a redeemed invite can't be revoked.

post.summary: Creates a credential for a subject.
post.description:
Generated secrets are shown only once. Idempotent on a caller-chosen `id`:
repeating the request with the same content returns 200, and for a secret
key generates new secrets for both slots and shows those, so the first
ones stop working.

200.description: Already existed with the same content. A secret key's new secrets are in `secret_keys`.

201.description: Created. A secret key's secrets are in `secret_keys`, shown only once.

Batch.description: Control-plane operations to apply in order, all or nothing.

idempotency_key.description:
Chosen by the caller, so that repeating the batch answers what it
first answered instead of applying it again. Remembered per caller,
for committed batches only. At most 255 characters.

idempotency_seconds.description:
How long to remember the key, up to the server's maximum (an hour
unless configured otherwise); the server's default (ten minutes)
when absent.

BatchMethod.description: The methods a batch accepts: only writes.

body.description: The operation's request body, if it takes one.

path.description:

optional query string.

BatchResult.description: One operation's answer, as it would have answered alone.

body.description: The operation's response body, including its own `cursor`.

BatchResults.description: What every operation of a committed batch answered, in order.

Check.description: One check a decision makes besides the required actions.

ClientKind.description: Whether the session's refresh token travels in a cookie or in bodies.

Contribution.description: One policy that bears on an action, and where it lands.

policy.description: The policy's action or group, as written.

Cursor.description:
The position of an event in the change feed.
